who: townsfolk, stallholders and the steward's people, about goods the player brought to the town

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} came in with carts of {good} and asked nothing for it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Nothing yet. Folk who give freely send the bill later.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My children ate tonight because of {player}'s {good}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then say so in the temple. Loudly. Let the keep hear it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Gifts of {good} from {player}. What's the price, I wonder?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A vote at the Moot. A blind eye at the gate. Something.

lines.speaker: C
lines.text: Or some folk just give. Drink your ale.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {steward} has written {player}'s {good} into the granary book twice.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Twice?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Once for the town. Once for {lord}'s pride. He hates owing strangers.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} unloading {good} with their own hands. A champion, hauling crates.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Lords don't lift crates. That's why we cheer champions and not lords.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Heard {player} brought forty wagons of {good}. Enough to feed the hold a year.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I unloaded it. Six carts, and one with a cracked axle.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Six is still six more than {lord} sent.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Free {good} in a Fed town. My stall's price just halved.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Charity for them, ruin for us. Put that in your prayers.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player}'s {good}? I'd not feed it to the pigs.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Pigs aren't proud, {A}. Neither am I, this winter.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} left {good} at the gate with their bounty still unpaid.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Guards took the carts and let the driver run. Fair trade, they said.

who: townsfolk, the steward's clerks, outlaws and clergy, about coin the player gave to the town or stole from it

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Coin from {player} in the town chest. Or out of it. Depends who's telling.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Either way it's the town's coin, and somebody's grinning.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} gave the town purse three hundred in silver.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: {steward} wept. First time the books have balanced since the Breaking.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Why would a drifter pour coin into {town}?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Friends are cheaper bought than lords. They know that.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The councillor put their own silver in the chest before the vote.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Clever. Hard to argue with someone spending their own coin first.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Counting-room strongbox. Empty. Lock picked clean as a bone.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: {player} again. {lord} wants a rope this time, not a fine.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Town purse is light again. Work on the gate has stopped.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Stolen, they say. By {player}, they say. Watch your own belt.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} lifted the town's coin right under the steward's nose.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Pour them a cup when they come. {band} never forgets a good thief.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The alms went with the town coin. {player} took the lot.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then we pray for their soul. And nail the poor box to the floor.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Heard {player} took a thousand from the keep and killed two guards.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Heard it from the guards, did you? Both of them drinking yonder.

who: townsfolk, guards and the keep's household, about the player arriving in town

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player}'s in {town}. Came in by the east road.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then lock up, or lay a place. I can't tell which yet.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} walked straight through our gate. With a price on their head.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Ring the bell. Or wait till they've drunk enough to be slow.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Look who's at the well. {player}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Don't sell them so much as a turnip. Let them move on.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player}'s taken the room over the stables.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I'll sleep with my knife, then. Pass the bread.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: New face. {player}, they call themselves.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Guild sort, by the boots. Sell them something overpriced.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player}'s back in {town}! Warm the good cider.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And tell your sister to stop fussing with her hair.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} rides in and the guards stand straighter than for {lord}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then don't let {lord} see it. He counts these things.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player}'s banner on the road. Lord of a hall now.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Bow or not? I never know with new-made lords.

lines.speaker: C
lines.text: Bow. It costs nothing, and their memories are long.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Councillor {player} is in town. The council sits tonight, then.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: {steward} will be hiding the ledgers already.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player}'s here with an army, they say. Two hundred spears.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Two companions and a lame mule. I saw them come in.

who: hamlet folk, the keep's household, outlaws and priests, about the player retaking a lost hamlet

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {hamlet} is ours again. {player} drove them out.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then someone had better sow it before winter.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My cousin sleeps in her own bed in {hamlet} tonight.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Because {player} did what {lord}'s heroes wouldn't. Remember that at the Moot.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {lord} is pleased about {hamlet}. Publicly.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And privately?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Privately he asks why a drifter is doing a hero's work.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} retook {hamlet} with a handful. The songs are already starting.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Songs won't rebuild a burned barn. Still, I'll sing.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: We held {hamlet} two weeks. Then {player} came.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Lost good men there. Next time we see that face, no talking.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} took {hamlet} back. Who's going to hold it?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Nobody. Three raids and it's empty again. Watch.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say {player} cut down every outlaw in {hamlet} with one blade.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Outlaws walked off when they saw the torches. My brother watched from the ditch.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: We'll need to bless the wells at {hamlet} before anyone drinks.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Thank {player} after. The saints first, then the sword.

who: guild members, townsfolk and priests, about the player clearing a monster lair

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} cleared the lair past the ridge. Nothing's come out since.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Nothing yet. Those holes always fill again.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: One less nest feeding the Blight. {player} went in with three and came out with three.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Better than {guild}. {guild} comes out with two.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} took a lair off our board. Our contract, our coin.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Should've gone yourself. {guild} sat on it a month.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's the fourth lair {player}'s burned out this season.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And no leak near {town} since spring. That's no accident.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} cleared the den. Did anyone bless the place after?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No priest goes out there, {A}. Not even you.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} killed {calamity}, they're saying. With their own hands.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It was a nest of rats with Blight in their fur. Big rats, mind.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Clearing lairs now. Building a name before they ask for something.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Let them ask. The lair's still empty.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Lair's cleared. The grain carts can use the north track again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: If there's any grain left to cart.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Bounty on their head, and {player} still clears our lairs.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Clever. A bounty's harder to collect off a hero.

who: families, the keep's household and outlaws, about the player signing someone into their company

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} signed on another one for their company.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Growing, that company. Somebody ought to count them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Our boy's gone with {player}. Made his mark this morning.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Better a sword under a decent captain than a sickle under a bad lord.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Our daughter signed with {player}. Not a word to me first.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: She'll come back with coin or not at all. That's the road.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} is taking our best young men. {lord} has noticed.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Fewer mouths for the granary.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fewer spears for the levy, too.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} signed a lad we'd been courting for weeks.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Better pay than ours, I suppose. And no rope at the end.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player}'s raising an army to take the empty throne.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Five people and a cook isn't an army, {A}.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Every lad in {town} wants a place with {player}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And every mother wants them home. Mothers lose.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Who'd join {player}? Only those with nothing left.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then they'll find plenty of company in that company.

who: guild members, sellswords and the keep's household, about the player hiring a sellsword or guildsman

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} hired a blade out of {guild}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Coin buys a blade. It doesn't buy the back behind it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} paid {guild}'s best for a month. Good wage.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Good wage, but they'll lead from the front. Our veteran won't like that.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hiring swords. {player} means to go somewhere bad.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The Broken March, I'd wager. Pray they come back.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A drifter hiring swords inside {lord}'s walls.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: {lord} hires the Grey Company and calls it policy. When {player} does it, it's a threat.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} hired one of the Red Lances. Paid in advance.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: In advance? Then they're mad or honest. Rare, either way.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say {player} bought the whole Grey Company.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: One Grey Company man. And he's half deaf.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sellswords still take {player}'s coin. Even now.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Sellswords would serve the Demon King if he paid in silver.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} hires sellswords for their hall. Like any lord.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Like any lord. That's what worries the other lords.

who: townsfolk, families and guild members, about the player sending recruits out on a task

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player}'s people rode out at dawn on some errand.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Errands with spears. I'd like to know where.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Saw {player}'s lot on the road, marching tidy as a lord's guard.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Without {player}? They trust their people, then.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} sends the recruits out and stays by the fire.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's what captains do. Lords do the same from a keep.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} sent my son to the Broken March. Didn't go themselves.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Pray, then. And send him a letter, if someone there can read it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player}'s recruits took the lair job before {guild} could post it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Cheap swords beating the guild. That's how guilds end.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Recruits of {player}'s on the east track. Green as grass.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Leave them. They're bait. Their master's behind them somewhere.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Heard {player}'s recruits all drowned in the fens.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Two blisters and a lost boot. They're at the inn now.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player}'s people went to {hamlet} before {lord}'s garrison had its boots on.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Don't say it so loud. The sergeants are sore enough.

who: townsfolk, the garrison and outlaws, about the player giving their recruits standing orders

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player}'s given their people standing orders. Patrol, guard, haul.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Orders that hold while the captain's away. That's a proper company.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player}'s recruits walk the road to {hamlet} twice a day now.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Raiders keep off. I'll take it, whoever's orders they are.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player}'s people patrol our roads under their own orders.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's the garrison's duty. And the garrison's pride.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {lord} will say something. Or the sergeants will, with fists.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: One of {player}'s told me to shift my cart off the track.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Did he now? Who made him warden of the road?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player}'s lot guard the carts now. Same hours every day.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Same hours means we know when they're not there.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say {player} ordered their men to tax the hamlets.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Ordered them to dig a latrine. I heard the groaning myself.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player}'s recruits keep the market watch. Not a purse cut all week.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: My cousin the cutpurse has taken up honest work out of boredom.

who: masons, townsfolk and the keep's household, about the player building part of their hall

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player}'s building again. Another wing on that hall.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Stone costs. Somebody in {town} is getting rich off it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} pays the masons weekly, in silver. I've had worse masters.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Haven't had better. Cut it square and keep your mouth shut.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A storehouse at {player}'s hall now. Full, they say.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Full storehouses draw raiders like honey draws wasps.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} has raised a barracks. Walls, towers, cots for thirty.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Thirty spears outside town. Comfort or worry, I can't decide.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {lord} watched the hall go up from the tower this morning.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: With what face?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The face he keeps for rival claimants.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player}'s putting an alchemy lab in that hall.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The Littles will be livid. Forty years they've sold every draught in Stonepass.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say {player}'s hall has a gilded roof.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Slate. Leaks in the east corner, too. I laid it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A council seat and a hall. {player} has more rooms than {lord}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Don't say that near the keep, or you'll have none.

who: townsfolk, guild members, masons and the keep's household, about the player as councillor spending the town's surplus

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The council spent the surplus. {player}'s motion.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: On what?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Walls, mostly. And an expedition east.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} carried the vote. Walls before winter.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: {steward} wanted a feast for the Moot. Walls are cheaper than funerals.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The town's surplus gone on walls, and grain's still dear.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Walls don't eat. People do. Tell your councillor that.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} paid for an expedition to the March out of the town chest.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Good. {guild} bleeds and the town pays. That's how it ought to be.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A councillor spending {lord}'s surplus without asking him.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The town's surplus, {lady} says. Not his.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Don't let him hear you agree with her.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Walls! While we eat bark. {player} spends like we're Thriving.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The walls kept raiders off the granary. That's why we still have bark.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say {player} took half the surplus for their own hall.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The steward's book says every penny went into the stones.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Books lie. Stones don't.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Council's ordered towers. {player} wants them up before harvest.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then I'll need every mason in {town}, and their apprentices besides.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That one sits on our council and spends our coin. How?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Bought the seat, or earned it before the trouble. Either way, we're stuck.

who: guards, victims, outlaws and clergy, about the player paying off their bounty

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} paid off their bounty. Clean slate.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A slate wiped clean still remembers the chalk.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Paid in full at the keep. Coin on the table, no haggling.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Stolen coin paying for stolen coin. The steward didn't ask.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Take down {player}'s notice. They've paid.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Pity. I'd a good likeness of their face on it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} paid {lord}. Not me. Not for my burnt barn.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The law minds the lord's purse, {A}. Not your barn.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} bought their way back into the towns.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Gone soft. Or gone clever. Watch which.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Bounty's paid. {player}'s welcome at my stall again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Count your coins after they leave, all the same.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say {player} paid the bounty with a lord's signet ring.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Plain silver. The clerk bit every coin, and nearly a tooth.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Paying a bounty mends the law. Not the soul.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Let the law have its coin. We'll have the rest.

who: townsfolk, sergeants, victims and outlaws, about the player working off a bounty in a labour gang

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player}'s in the labour gang. Breaking stone for the town.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Good. Let them sweat for what they owe.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Watched {player} haul stone all day under the sergeant's eye.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Didn't run? I'd have run.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Nowhere to run with that much bounty.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That one in the gang works harder than the paid men.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's {player}. Owes {lord} a small fortune.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Bounty gang's ahead of the steward's schedule. {player} drives them.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A felon leading the gang. Don't tell {steward}.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} digs our ditch now. Won't give back my brother's cart.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No. But the ditch keeps the flood off your barley.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Our old friend {player}, digging ditches for {lord}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Shackled and smiling. Broke, more like.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player}'s chained in the keep's dungeon, they say.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: They're on the road gang. Waved at me this morning.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Bring {player} bread when the gang breaks at noon.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The sergeant won't like it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The sergeant ate my bread last week.

who: priests, monks and townsfolk, about the player undertaking a priest's atonement task

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} went to the priests for atonement.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And what did the priests ask?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Something hard. They always do.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} knelt at the altar all night. Never slept.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Kneeling's easy. The task we set them is not.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} begged atonement with a bounty still unpaid.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then let them pay the lord first. The saints don't take stolen silver.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Atonement! After what {player} did to us?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The priests forgive. The market remembers.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A barrow cleansing for their penance. {player} came back grey to the bone.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The dead don't like visitors. Light a candle for them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} wants absolution. Let them come ask us.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: We're not saints, {A}. We don't have to forgive.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say {player} whipped themselves bloody on the pilgrim road.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Flagellants whip. {player} carried water at the hospice. Quietly.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Brother William offered to hear {player}'s confession himself.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: He never offers. What does he want with them?

who: hungry townsfolk, the keep's household, outlaws, clergy and caravaneers, about the player burning the town's granary

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The granary's burned. They say it was {player}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then we'll eat their name this winter. There's nothing else.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No caravans for weeks. Nobody trades with a town that burns.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: {player} did this. If I see them, I'll do worse.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The children asked what's for supper. I said ash.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Pray {lord}'s men find {player} before winter does.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {steward} says we're down to seed corn.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then hang the arsonist from the granary's black beams. {lord} insists.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} burned the granary. Starving towns are easy towns.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Blackbeard will want that one at his fire.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No penance is big enough for burning a town's bread.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then we pray for the hungry. Let the lord pray for vengeance.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say {player} burned half of {town} with the granary.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Only the granary. The smoke made it look like the town.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Only? There's no only about bread.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Turn the carts. {town}'s granary is ash, and nobody trades into a fire.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: We'll come back when they've starved quiet.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Some say the fire was {player}. Some say a Crow arsonist.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Either way, we're Lean all year.

who: craftsmen, guild members, outlaws and clergy, about the player stealing from the workshops

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Somebody stripped the workshops in the night. {player}'s name came up.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It always comes up, after the fact.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My best chisels, gone. A lifetime to temper them.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: {player} won't know what they're worth. That's the insult.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Bar the shutters. {player}'s back in town.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Bars didn't stop them last time.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} robbed the smithy and sold the blades to {guild}'s green recruits.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So I bought my own sword back off a thief. Lovely.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} cleaned out three workshops in one night. Proper work.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Proper folly. Crafters talk. Every gate will have that face.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say {player} carried off the master smith's anvil.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: An anvil? On their back? Through the gate?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Well. That's how I heard it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The weaver came begging. {player} took a season's cloth off her loom.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Give her the alms. And her name for the prayers.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Funny how {good} is cheap on the stalls since the robbery.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Funny how you're buying it.

who: outlaws, travellers, the keep's household and farm folk, about the player joining or strengthening an outlaw camp, or killing outlaws

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player}'s been out at the outlaw camps. Doing what, nobody agrees.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Killing them or joining them. Out there it looks the same.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} rides with {band} now. Saw them at the ford.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then the road to {hamlet} is closed to me.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} brought us three men and a cart of arrows.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Give them a seat by the fire. Near the king.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {band} grows by the week. {player}'s doing.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Past thirty, and {lord} sends a hero. Let it grow.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} broke {band}'s camp. Eleven dead.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The road's quiet. I'll take quiet.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} killed my brother at the camp.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then blood is owed. {band} doesn't forget.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Our champion broke {band} before {lord}'s heroes had saddled up.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The heroes will sulk for a week.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} killed {band}'s king and wears his crown now.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Outlaw kings don't have crowns. They have hats. Bad ones.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Outlaws dead at the camp. {player}, they say.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Some were farm lads from {hamlet}. Hungry ones.

who: guild members, families and the keep's household, about the player murdering guild members

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {guild} lost a member. Knifed. Folk whisper {player}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Don't whisper it in the guild tavern.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} killed one of ours. Their name's on the board by noon.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No contract fee. Every blade in {guild} will do it for free.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A guildsman dead, and {player} seen leaving the alley.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Seen? Or said to be seen?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {lord} won't put a price on {player}. The guild will do it for him.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Cheaper that way. And no blood on the keep's steps.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} killed a guild hunter. One less on our trail.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And a whole guild more on theirs.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {dead}'s mother keeps setting out his plate.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: {player} owes her a son. Owes all of us something.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say {player} killed a whole party of five.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: One. And he drew first, the barman swears.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: We buried {dead} today. The guild paid for the stone.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And {player} paid for the grave, in a manner of speaking.

who: craftsmen, rivals, the keep's household and clergy, about the player murdering a craftsman

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {dead} the craftsman is dead. {player}'s name is on every tongue.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And the title passes to some lesser hand.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {dead} is gone, and I'm the best smith left in the hold.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Don't smile like that. Folk will think you paid {player}.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: His tools are still warm on the bench.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Who'll finish his orders? Who'll feed his apprentices?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} murdered a maker. No smith will sell them a nail.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Let them fight with their fingernails.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {good}'s gone up. {dead} made half of what was sold.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A maker dies. Everyone pays.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {lord} had blades ordered from {dead}. Paid half up front.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then {lord} is out half a purse and a weaponsmith. He won't forgive it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say a rival paid {player} to do it. Fifty coin.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Or it was over a bent buckle. Nobody knows. That's worse.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {dead} carved our altar rail. Now we pray at his grave.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The Temple should ask why. Before the lord's men ask how.

who: peasants, the keep's household and outlaws, about the player levying men or coin as a titled lord

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} called a levy. Men or coin, your choice.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Same as any lord, then. Didn't take long.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My two sons, or twelve coin. That's {player}'s levy.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Pay the coin. Sons are harder to make.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player}'s levy is lighter than {lord}'s ever was.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: This year. Lords learn quickly.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Levy-men came. {player}'s seal on the paper.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A drifter's seal. We bowed to nobody and got this.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} levied men from hamlets that already owe {lord}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Two lords, one harvest. Someone will starve, and it won't be them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player}'s levy sent three farm lads straight to our fire.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Give them bows. Thank {player} kindly when we meet.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player}'s taking every man under fifty, I heard.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Five men from the whole hold. My cousin read the notice out.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: If {player} calls the levy, I'll march. They've marched for us.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: More than once. More than {lord} ever has.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The levy takes the tithe-payers too. The temple will feel it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then pray the lords fight less and plough more.

who: stallholders, shoppers and the steward's people, about the player buying in the market and moving prices

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} bought up the {good} at market.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: All of it?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Near enough. Price jumped by noon.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} bought every sack of {good} while we go hungry.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: To sell back at double, I'd wager. I'll remember it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} pays whatever I ask. So I've started asking more.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's how you lose a good customer, {A}.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} bought my whole stall, then gave half to the beggars.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Generous or showing off? Either way the beggars ate.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A stranger cornering {good} in Sunward. The Coin won't like it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The Coin will buy them, or bury them. He always does.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} bought the whole market, stalls and all.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Three barrels. The rest is ale talking.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The councillor buys {good} by the cartload. Ahead of a shortage?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then {steward} should be buying too. Quietly.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sold {good} to {player}. My neighbours won't look at me.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Coin's coin. But wash it before you spend it.

who: stallholders, rivals and the steward's people, about the player selling goods in the market and moving prices

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} dumped a load of {good} on the market.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Prices fell like a stone down a well.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} undercut me on {good}. My stall's dead this week.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Undercut them back. Or join them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Cheap {good} at last. {player} sold near cost.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Near cost for them is a feast for us.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Glut of {good}. {player} sold into a full market.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Fool's trade. Should've carted it to a lean town.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {steward} bought {player}'s {good} for the granary.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: At what price?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fair. Which is rare, from either of them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player}'s selling Blight-salt, they say. Grey stuff.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Plain salt. I tasted it. Salt.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Where'd {player} get that much {good}?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Off a cart. Off someone else's cart.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Stranger sold {good} cheap and Reedwatch cheered.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: We cheer anything cheap. That's Reedwatch's whole charm.

who: stallholders, victims, scholars and the keep's household, about the player selling a single fine item

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} sold a fine piece at market today.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Loot, I'd wager. Fine pieces don't grow on the road.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} sold me a blade with a guild mark scratched off.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then don't wear it near the guild tavern.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got a good cloak off {player}. Fair price, no haggling.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: They haggle hard with merchants. Soft with us.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A ring from a March fort, sold in {town}'s own market.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Old crown work. {lord} will want it before the Moot.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's my husband's sword on {player}'s table.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Off his body, or off the outlaws who killed him? Ask before you shout.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say {player} sold a shard of the Warden's Blade.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A rusty dagger and a bent helm. I was there.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} sold the library a ledger from the March forts.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Stewards' hand. Before the Breaking. Did they know what they had?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Lovely brooch. {player} won't say where it came from.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then it came from a grave or a purse. Pass.

who: horse traders, outlaws and townsfolk, about the player buying a horse or cart

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} bought a horse at the market.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then they'll be gone by tomorrow. Riders never stay.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sold {player} the grey mare. Paid without haggling.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The grey? She bites.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Didn't mention it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} bought a cart. A trader now, is it?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Or a thief who needed a bigger sack.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Good to see {player} on a proper horse. They walked too long.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Long roads, bad feet. Walking does that.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fine horse on the east road. {player}'s.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Fine horses get stolen. Ask the Dust Riders.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} bought a warhorse fit for a king.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A plough horse with ambition. I sold it to them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Bought a horse. Means they can run faster next time.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Or arrive faster. Bar the door.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player}'s bought a cart for the wounded. Rides with the guild parties.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A champion with a sickcart. The old Stewards did that.

who: smiths, miners, fellers and townsfolk, about the player buying better tools

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} bought new tools from the smith.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Good tools, good work. Or good burglary.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} paid full price for my best picks.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Full price? You must have doubled it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Doubled it. They still paid.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} turned up at the mine with a shiny new pick.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: New pick, soft hands. Give it a week.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} bought axes for the whole grove crew.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then we'll fell more by Sunday and drink it by Monday.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say {player} bought sky-iron tools from the refiners.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Plain steel. The sky-iron secret isn't sold to strangers.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Pry bars and cold chisels. What's {player} building?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Or breaking into. Watch the counting-house.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} buys the tools and leaves them at the hall for the workmen.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A lord who buys the picks. Haven't seen one of those.

who: guild members, townsfolk and contract-sellers, about the player taking a contract

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} took a contract off the board.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Which one?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The one nobody else would touch.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} took the {hamlet} job before {guild} could field a party.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Quicker than our five. And cheaper.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player}'s taken the wolf job at {hamlet}. My sister's folds are safe.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Wolves are the lord's beasts. Hope {player} knows the charter.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A sealed contract from the keep. {player} took it unread.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That kind ends in a ditch.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Juliana Carter sold {player} a contract. She sells to anyone.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then let's hope it's an honest one, for once.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} took a contract on a lord's life, I heard.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A contract to guard salt carts. Dull, but it pays.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Do they finish their contracts, this {player}?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Every one. {guild} keeps a tally, and it's an annoying tally.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} takes contracts against us now. Guild coin.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then we take one against them. Hollow Knives come cheap.

who: miners, fellers and foremen, about the player labouring at a mine or grove

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} worked the mine with us all day.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Didn't faint? Wonders.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} swung a pick beside me. Kept pace, too.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Mind they don't keep yours. Picks walk off.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Why's a champion breaking ore?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Coin's coin, {A}. Even heroes eat.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} felled three oaks before noon at the grove.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Nothing common about that axe-arm. Stand well back.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} works for wages and never grumbles.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then hire them again. Grumblers we have plenty.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} found a seam of silver in the mine, they say.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A seam of mud. The silver's in your head.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player}'s at the grove, watching the paths, not the trees.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Scouting for someone. Keep an eye out.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A titled lord in the mine. Shovelling.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Don't laugh. Ironhand did the same, they say, in his youth.

who: smiths, families, the keep's household and outlaws, about the player arming their recruits

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} armed their recruits. New spears all round.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Somebody's getting ready for something.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} ordered twenty spearheads. Paid half up front.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Half's more than {lord} ever pays up front.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player}'s company in mail now. Better kit than our garrison.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: {lord} will want to know where the coin came from.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My lad wears a helmet now. {player} bought it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Better a helmet than a hood, out east.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player}'s recruits have new crossbows.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then we stop ambushing them. Ambush someone poorer.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say {player}'s men wear enchanted steel.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Boiled leather, painted grey. Wouldn't fool a smith's boy.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} armed their people properly. No farm lads with pitchforks.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Shame {lord} won't do the same for the levy.

who: innkeepers, drinkers and townsfolk, about the player earning wages

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} drew wages today.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Spent them by nightfall, I'd guess.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player}'s buying rounds. Wage day.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then sit near them. Drink while it lasts.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} earned good coin at the wharf. Gave half to the widow.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Which widow?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The one with the leaking roof.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Wage labour suits {player}. Didn't look like it would.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Everybody's a labourer once.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} earning honest wages? There's a trick in it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Maybe honesty is the trick. Rare enough to look like one.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} earned a hundred coin in a day, they say.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Twelve. I counted it out myself.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Who'd pay {player} wages?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Someone who couldn't get anyone else.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A councillor drawing labourer's wages. What's that for?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: To show the hall they're no lord. Or to look like it.

who: families, clergy, scholars and the keep's household, about the player sending a mage or healer to the tower school by Mereworth

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} sent someone to the tower school by Mereworth.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A mage? From here?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A healer, they say.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} paid for our girl to go to the tower.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: She'll come back talking like a scholar and correcting your sums.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Another healer sent to the tower instead of the temple.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The tower teaches herbs. The temple teaches mercy. We need both.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player}'s training mages. A court mage in waiting.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: {lord} keeps his own mages close. He won't like a rival's.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} sent the cooper's boy to the tower. Spark in his hands.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Margaret the Sage saw it first, they say.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say {player} is sending warlocks to the tower.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A healer and a herbwife. Hardly the last spring.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Why pay for a mage's schooling?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Mages who owe you are worth an army.

lines.speaker: C
lines.text: Strictly, half an army. The tower graduates barely a hundred a year.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player}'s coin sent the tanner's son to Mereworth.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then let him learn to wash it off.

who: lodge hunters, shepherds and the lord's foresters, about the player joining the hunting lodge

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} paid their dues and joined the lodge.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Swore the Half Law, then. Let's see them keep it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Twenty-five coin and an oath. {player}'s one of us.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: One of us till the charter bites. Then we'll see.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} joined the lodge. {lord}'s foresters are watching.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Watch the wolves, then. That's where the charter breaks.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player}'s lodge now. Maybe they'll cull the wolves off our folds.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Charter says no. But {player} doesn't strike me as a charter sort.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Take half. Leave half. Did they say it like they meant it?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Said it like a farmer counting sheep. They'll do.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say {player} is lodge-master already.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Dues paid this morning. Master by nightfall? Hardly.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} joined the lodge. They'll be in our poaching woods now.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then hunt the far side of the stream. Same as always.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The King's Lodge took {player}. Isabella Fox will want their vote.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: For Sir Robert's banner? The old master would sooner burn it.

who: lodge hunters, stallholders and townsfolk, about the player selling hides and meat through the lodge

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} sold hides through the lodge.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Lodge took its cut. Fair dealing.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player}'s hides put the lodge purse over four hundred.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then the town gets the rest. Shame, that.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} sells through the lodge, not through my stall.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Lodge cut's lower than your markup, {A}.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Good hides from {player}. Clean skinning, no holes.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Someone taught them right. Or they ruined a lot learning.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} sells meat to the lodge, not to the Coin's buyers.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Good. The Coin buys cheap and sells it on at double.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} brought in a wolf pelt. Charter breaker!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A dog's pelt. From a dead dog. Calm yourself.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Where did {player} hunt all that? Not our woods past half, I hope.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Counted the herd myself. Half left standing. They keep the Law.

who: lodge hunters, families and the keep's household, about the player hiring a hunter away from the lodge

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} hired a lodge hunter. Took them off our rota.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Forty coin. The lodge will remember.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} hired our best bow for a month. We're a crew short.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And the far hunt's due. Who goes in her place?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Our son's off with {player}, hunting for coin.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Better coin than lodge pay. Worse odds, maybe.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} hires lodge huntsmen for their own hunts now.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Hunting what? Not the lord's beasts, if they're wise.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Half price for lodge members. {player} paid full anyway.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then they're a good one. Or bad at sums.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say {player} hired the whole lodge to break the charter.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: One hunter. To find a lost mule.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player}'s got a lodge tracker now. Hunting our camp, I'd guess.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then we move the fire tonight. Trackers hate wet ground.

who: freed families, clergy, outlaws and the keep's household, about the player raiding the slavers' holds

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} raided the slavers' holds in the north.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Raided them? And lived?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My sister came home last night. {player} broke the pen.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then light a candle for {player}. Two.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} freed the captives. The saints smile on that.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And the slavers will hunt them for it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The slaver camp west of Stonepass is burnt. {player}'s work.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Ironhand never lifted a finger to them. Now a stranger has.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {lord} pays ransoms, and {player} burns the pens. Awkward for the keep.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Awkward is cheaper than ransom.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} hit the slavers. Even we don't touch those holds.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Even we have limits. Good on them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say {player} killed all thirty-six slavers single-handed.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Six, with help. The rest ran north.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Another reason they're our champion.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Champions wait for orders. This one doesn't.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} raiding slavers? After everything?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Maybe they're trying to pay something back. Let them try.

who: families, clergy, outlaws and the keep's household, about the player ransoming captives

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} paid the ransom for the captives.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Paid slavers. That feeds the trade.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Our daughter's home. {player} paid what we couldn't.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then we owe them. And we pay our debts.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Ransoming captives is mercy, even if it feeds slavers.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Mercy now, justice later. The order matters.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} paid the slavers? Must have dealings with them.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Or a heart. Rare thing, but it happens.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} ransomed {hamlet}'s people before {lord} could.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: He'll say he meant to. Next week.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} paid a thousand for the captives, they say.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Ninety. The slavers wanted more, but the captives were thin.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} pays ransoms. Means captives are worth taking.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Don't, {A}. We're thieves. Not that.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Saw the ransomed folk come down the road with {player} beside the cart.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Walking, not riding. Gave their horse to an old man.

who: victims' families, clergy, outlaws and the keep's household, about the player selling captives to the slavers

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} sold captives to the slavers.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then {player} is dead to {town}. Spit on the name.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No caravans. No trade. Because {player} sold people.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Every road knows it. The whole town pays for one sin.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My husband, sold north by {player}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: We'll find him. Or we'll find {player}.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The temple doors are barred to {player}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And the hearth, and the inn, and the gate.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Even {band} won't sell people. {player} did.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then {player}'s worse than us. Never thought I'd say that.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say {player} sold a whole hamlet north.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Three outlaws they'd caught. Still a slaver's deal. Still foul.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {lord} will hang {player} at the gate if they show their face.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Ironhand has sworn the same. Every lord has.

who: merchants, families and clergy, about the player trading with the slavers' holds

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} trades with the slavers' holds.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then nothing from {player}'s carts touches my table.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Caravans skip {town}. {player} traded with slavers here.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Weeks of empty markets for one person's greed.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player}'s carts came down from the north. From the holds.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Burn the carts. Wash your hands after.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: In Sunward money's money. Even slavers' money.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Not even the Coin trades in people. Not openly.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Did they see our cousins up there, at the holds?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: If they did, they didn't buy them back.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say {player} owns a slavers' hold now.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Bought salt from one. Bad enough.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} came to the altar for a blessing on their trade.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: We bless nothing that comes down from the north holds.

who: hamlet folk, guild members, clergy and the keep's household, about the player stopping a Blight leak from a lair

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} stopped a Blight leak at the lair.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Before it reached {hamlet}? Thank the saints.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The pack never reached {hamlet}. {player} was waiting for it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: My cow lives another week.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That leak was ours to stop. {guild} was three weeks late.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: {player} wasn't.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The Blight turned back. {player} carried holy water, they say.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Holy water, and a very sharp sword.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} stops one leak and wants thanking.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then thank them. Leaks don't stop themselves.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} sealed a rift for good, they say.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A leak, not a rift. The rift's still there, still hungry.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {lord} meant to send heroes. {player} went first.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The heroes are at the hunt. Again.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The wanted one stopped the leak. Strange.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The Blight doesn't care about bounties. Neither did they, it seems.

who: wildcrafters, outlaws and the tower watch, about the player climbing a cliff to a lookout or cache

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} climbed the cliff to the old lookout.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Mad or brave. Same thing, up there.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} climbed the butte-top and brought down an armful of herbs.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Wildcrafters do that. Did they fall?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Not once.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} found our cache on the cliff.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then move it. Higher.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} climbed up to the beacon on the ridge.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Did they light it?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Looked east a long while. Didn't say a word.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say {player} climbed so high they touched the clouds.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A cliff. A tall one. With a goat path halfway.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Why climb to a lookout? What's up there?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A view of our roads. Who's on them, and who isn't.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} climbs cliffs like a herd boy. With a hall to run.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Old Stewards climbed to the Rim lookouts too. Maybe that's the point.

who: families, craftsmen, the garrison and townsfolk, about someone from the town joining the player's company

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} has taken on another follower.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: From {town}? Who?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The tanner's lad. Quick hands.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My brother joined {player}'s company. Proud day.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Proud and worried. Both at once.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My apprentice left the bench for {player}'s company.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Swords pay better than shoes, {A}.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} took on the sergeant's daughter.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The sergeant will be furious. Or proud. Hard to tell with him.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} took one of {lord}'s guards into their company.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Desertion, the sergeant calls it. Promotion, the guard calls it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say {player} recruited one of {lord}'s heroes.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The cook from this inn. Best stew in {town}, gone.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Who signs with {player}? Fools and runaways.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And folk with debts in {town}. Check the tally sticks.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} took Agnes's boy. He's never held a spear.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: He will by the week's end. They train them hard, I hear.
